sa_market_summary: The Hyundai ix35 was one of the most popular compact SUVs in South Africa during its run, offering strong value versus competitors like the Nissan Qashqai and Ford Kuga. Sold here from 2010 until it was replaced by the Tucson in 2016/2017, the ix35 built a large used-car footprint. It comes in both 2WD and AWD configurations, with petrol and diesel engine options. Hyundai's 5-year/100,000km warranty covered new units, and some early second-owner examples may still carry residual coverage. Parts availability from Hyundai dealers and independent suppliers is good, though diesel components carry higher repair costs.

known_faults.fault: Timing chain rattle (2.0 GDi petrol engine)
known_faults.description: The 2.0-litre GDi petrol engine is known for timing chain stretch and tensioner wear. A cold-start rattle that clears after a few seconds is the primary warning sign. Left unattended, a failed timing chain causes catastrophic engine damage.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Start the engine from cold and listen carefully for a rattling noise from the front of the engine in the first 10-15 seconds. Request full service history to verify oil changes every 10,000km with the correct 5W-30 fully synthetic oil. This fault alone should be a deal-breaker if no documented history exists.
known_faults.source: Hyundai SA technical service bulletins, SA independent workshop data, Cars.co.za ix35 owner reports

known_faults.fault: Rear wheel arch and sill rust
known_faults.description: Older ix35 units, particularly those in coastal or high-rainfall areas, develop rust along the rear wheel arches and lower sills. Surface rust can progress to structural rust if left untreated.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Inspect all four wheel arches closely, paying attention to seams and the lip where the arch meets the body. Check lower door sills and the underside of the boot floor. Any bubbling paint indicates active rust beneath the surface.
known_faults.source: SA used-car inspection reports, AutoTrader SA seller disclosures, WeBuyCars assessment data

known_faults.fault: Power steering pump whine and failure
known_faults.description: Hydraulic power steering pump wear presents as a high-pitched whine at full steering lock. Pump failure results in heavy steering. Fluid leaks from the pump or hose connections are common on high-mileage examples.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Turn the steering wheel to full lock in both directions while stationary and listen for whining or groaning. Check the power steering fluid reservoir for correct level and look for signs of fluid leakage around the pump and hoses.
known_faults.source: SA motor spares suppliers, independent workshop reports

known_faults.description: AC compressor failure is reported on higher mileage ix35 units. A rattling or grinding noise when the AC is switched on indicates compressor bearing wear. Complete failure leaves the cabin without cooling.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Switch on the air conditioning and verify cold air within 60 seconds. Listen for any rattling or grinding from the compressor under the bonnet when AC is engaged. Check that the compressor clutch engages smoothly.
known_faults.source: SA AC specialist workshops, Hyundai SA owner community

known_faults.description: The 2.0 CRDi diesel variants are fitted with a DPF that requires regular motorway-speed driving to self-regenerate. Units used predominantly for short urban trips develop blocked DPFs, triggering a dashboard warning and reduced power.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Check for any DPF warning lights or engine management lights on the dashboard. Ask the seller about typical driving patterns. Request a diagnostic scan to check for stored DPF fault codes before purchasing.
known_faults.estimated_repair_zar: R3,000 - R8,000 (professional DPF clean) or R15,000 - R30,000 (replacement)
known_faults.source: Hyundai SA diesel service data, SA diesel specialist workshops

what_to_inspect_before_buying: Cold-start the engine and listen for timing chain rattle ,  walk away if present without documented repair history
Inspect all wheel arches and lower sills for rust, especially on 2010-2013 models
Test power steering at full lock in both directions for whining or groaning
Test air conditioning performance thoroughly ,  compressor replacement is expensive
For diesel variants, request a diagnostic scan and check for DPF-related fault codes
Verify service history with oil changes every 10,000km using correct synthetic oil
Check 4WD engagement on AWD models ,  engage and disengage while moving slowly in a safe area
Inspect underside for oil leaks and check gearbox for smooth shifting
Test all electric windows, mirrors, and central locking
owner_sentiment: Mixed to positive. ix35 owners appreciate the spacious interior, comfortable ride, and strong value for money at the used price point. The main concerns are the timing chain issue on petrol models and rust on older units. Diesel owners generally report good experiences if the vehicle has been used on longer runs. Hyundai SA parts and service support is adequate, though repair costs on the diesel can be high.
